title: Stage timeline component for Dedicated staged rollouts (gates + evidence drill-down + customer messaging)
creator: Marissa Cole
project: Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools
body:
Overview
We need a Console UI component that makes Dedicated staged rollouts understandable and safe to operate. This ticket covers the stage timeline UI (progress + states), gate status visualization, evidence drill-down, and customer-facing messaging for failures/holds/overrides.

This component will be used in two places:
1) Operator/Admin (Redwood internal + customer admins with rollout privileges) rollout detail page for a Dedicated pool.
2) Inline context inside “Promote stage” confirmation and “Gate failure” resolution flows.

Background / why
Dedicated customers are asking for safer upgrades (model version, runtime build, routing policy changes) without downtime. The rollout plan introduces explicit stages (e.g., 1% / 10% / 50% / 100% traffic or replica partitions). Operators need to know:
- What stage we’re on
- Whether gates passed/failed/unknown and why
- What the system did (auto-hold/auto-abort/rolled back)
- What actions are currently allowed (promote/abort/hold/force-promote)
- What the customer will see + what’s recorded in audit logs

Goals (UX)
- Make stage progression deterministic and readable (timeline: where we were, where we are, what’s next).
- Provide a consistent vocabulary for gate states (pass/fail/unknown/evaluating) and rollout states (draft/running/held/aborted/completed).
- Provide fast drill-down into “gate evidence” (metrics + time window + threshold + evaluation status + links to dashboards).
- Communicate failure/hold reasons with appropriate tone for customer admins (clear, non-alarming, action-oriented) while still surfacing operational truth.
- Keep the UI resilient to partial data (telemetry lag, missing tags) without showing an empty/blank experience.

Non-goals
- Designing a fully general experiment platform UI (beyond rollout safety).
- Designing arbitrary custom gate definitions UI for v1 (PM scope says Redwood-defined gate templates with limited config).

Primary personas
- Customer Admin / Platform Eng: wants to safely roll out changes without violating SLOs; needs clear “can I promote?” and “why not?” answers.
- Redwood SRE / Operator: needs quick diagnosis and safe/fast rollback/hold; needs links to deeper dashboards; needs to see override context and audit trail.

Key screens / placement
- Dedicated Pool → Rollouts → Rollout Plan Detail
  - Header summary (rollout state, current stage, target stage/version)
  - Stage timeline component (this ticket)
  - Gate evidence panel (drill-down)
  - Change history / audit trail link (DES-447)

Component spec: Stage timeline
1) Layout
- Horizontal timeline for up to ~8 stages; support responsive wrap to 2 rows if needed.
- Each stage is a “node” with:
  - Stage label: default “Stage 0 / Stage 1 …” plus traffic/partition descriptor (e.g., “1%”, “10%”, “50%”, “100%” or “2/20 replicas”).
  - Status icon (state-specific)
  - Gate summary indicator (mini pill or dot with tooltip)
  - Timestamp (optional; shown in hover or compact line under label)
- Connector line between nodes:
  - Solid when completed
  - Animated/active when current stage evaluating
  - Dashed when upcoming

2) Stage states (visual)
Stage state is distinct from gate state. Stage state is about progression; gate state is the health check result for promotion.

Stage state set (v1)
- Not started (upcoming)
  - Visual: neutral grey, no checkmark
- Active (current)
  - Visual: highlighted border + subtle pulse; connector animated
- Completed
  - Visual: filled/solid + checkmark
- Rolled back / reverted
  - Visual: “rewind/undo” icon; muted red outline; tooltip shows rollback reason
- Skipped (only if backend supports; if not, omit)
  - Visual: grey with slash; tooltip “Skipped by operator”

Rollout-level states impacting the component
- Held
  - Banner above timeline “Rollout held” and why; current stage node remains selected but shows “Hold” chip.
- Aborted
  - Timeline freezes; show terminal banner; emphasize “Traffic reverted to previous stable configuration”.
- Completed
  - Final node completed; show “Completed” chip with end timestamp.

3) Gate states (per stage)
Each stage has one “promotion gate evaluation” result aggregated across defined signals. Gate states shown as a small pill/dot on the stage node + a right-side panel when selected.

Gate state set (v1)
- Pass
  - Color: green; icon: check
  - Copy in tooltip: “All gates passed for this stage.”
- Fail
  - Color: red; icon: x
  - Tooltip: “One or more gates failed. Promotion blocked.”
- Evaluating
  - Color: blue/neutral; icon: spinner
  - Tooltip: “Evaluating gates over the last {window}. Requires {min samples}.”
- Unknown (missing/insufficient data)
  - Color: grey/amber; icon: question
  - Tooltip: “Gate status unknown due to missing or stale telemetry.”
- Not required (manual gate)
  - Color: grey; icon: person/hand
  - Tooltip: “Manual approval required. No automated gate evaluation configured.”

Important: “Unknown” must not look like “Pass”. It should be explicit that promotion may be blocked (likely fail-closed) depending on system policy.

4) Selection + drill-down
- Clicking a stage node selects it and opens the Gate Evidence side panel (or below on narrow screens).
- Default selection: current stage.
- Evidence panel includes:
  - Stage header: stage name + partition detail + start time
  - Gate summary: “Passing / Failing / Evaluating / Unknown” with brief reason
  - Evidence table with rows per signal (Error rate, p95/p99 latency, saturation/headroom, OOM rate, request drop/429, GPU health, optional quality regression)

Evidence row fields (display)
- Signal name
- Observed value (with unit)
- Threshold (with unit)
- Window (e.g., “last 15m”) and sample size if available
- Status (pass/fail/unknown)
- ‘View query’ (expand to show query text) (admin/internal only if needed)
- ‘Open dashboard’ link (Grafana/Redwood dashboards)

5) Actions area (contextual)
Actions should be near the timeline but clearly separated to avoid accidental promotion.
- Promote to next stage (primary)
- Abort rollout (danger)
- Hold rollout / Resume (secondary)
- Force promote (admin only; gated) (danger/secondary)

Action availability rules (UI logic; final source of truth is backend)
- Promote enabled only when:
  - Rollout state = running
  - Current stage gates = pass OR gate mode = manual + user confirmed checklist
  - Not within “no-promote” window (incident/high burn) (if backend returns a policy flag)
- Promote disabled when gates = fail/unknown/evaluating, with inline explanation.
- Force promote visible only when backend indicates user has permission AND rollout is in a promotable state (running or held) AND system policy allows force-promote.

Customer-facing messaging
We need copy that is:
- Precise (what happened)
- Blameless (avoid implying customer did something wrong)
- Actionable (what can they do next)

Banner / callout copy proposals
1) Held
Title: “Rollout is on hold”
Body (default): “Traffic remains on the current stage while we wait for a promotion decision.”
If gate-driven hold: “One or more gates did not meet the promotion criteria. Review evidence below.”
If operator hold: “An operator placed this rollout on hold. Reason: {reason}.”
CTA: “Resume rollout” (if allowed) / “Abort rollout” / “Contact support” (for customer admins)

2) Gate failed
Title: “Promotion blocked by gate failure”
Body: “This stage did not meet the promotion criteria. Traffic will not increase until gates pass or the rollout is aborted.”
Inline hint: “Most common causes: elevated error rate, latency regression, or saturation.”

3) Unknown / missing data
Title: “Gate status unknown”
Body: “We’re missing enough telemetry to evaluate promotion safely. This can happen during telemetry delays or tagging issues.”
Secondary line: “By default, promotion is blocked until data is available. Admins can override if needed.” (only show override clause to users who can see override)

4) Aborted
Title: “Rollout aborted”
Body: “Traffic has been reverted to the previous stable configuration.”
Optional: “Reason: {reason}”

5) Force promote
Confirmation modal (admin)
Title: “Force promote to {next stage}?”
Body: “This bypasses gate criteria and may impact latency, error rate, or capacity. This action is audited.”
Required input: reason text area (min 15 chars)
Checkbox: “I understand this may violate SLOs.”

6) Rollback / revert
If system performs auto-rollback (if supported):
Title: “Automatic rollback triggered”
Body: “We detected gate failures and reverted traffic to the previous stage to protect availability.”

Edge cases / UX requirements
- Multi-region pools: evidence should show region breakdown (collapsed by default). Timeline node remains global; evidence panel can show tabs or breakdown table.
- Small pools (few replicas): if stage partition is constrained, show a warning badge “Stage uses minimum partition size; results may be noisy.” (copy TBD).
- Streaming: if a rollback occurs, in-flight streams may continue. UI should show a subtle note for operators: “In-flight streaming requests may complete on the prior stage.” (only in admin/internal view if we decide to avoid confusing customers).
- Telemetry lag: show staleness indicator “Data delayed (~X min)” when backend includes watermark.
- Empty evidence: never show blank; show “We couldn’t load evidence for this stage” with retry + link to dashboards.

Accessibility
- Timeline nodes keyboard navigable (left/right arrows), Enter to select.
- Tooltips and status indicated with text not only color.
- Ensure contrast for red/green; use icons + labels.

Instrumentation (analytics)
- track: stage_selected (stage_id, rollout_id)
- track: evidence_row_expanded (signal)
- track: promote_clicked / aborted_clicked / hold_clicked / force_promote_clicked (role, rollout_state, gate_state)

Content / data contract assumptions (needs ENG alignment)
From Console backend (ENG-5980) we expect:
- rollout_state: draft | running | held | aborted | completed
- stages[]: stage_id, label, partition (percent/replicas), stage_state, gate_state, started_at, completed_at
- current_stage_id
- permissions: can_promote, can_abort, can_hold, can_force_promote
- gate_evidence endpoint: per stage with signal rows + window + observed + threshold + status + links

Links / references
- Confluence PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/dedicated-staged-rollouts-reserved-pools-prd.json
- Confluence Design Spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/staged-rollouts-for-dedicated-pools-design-spec.json
- Wireframe placeholder (observability): sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/observability/dedicated-rollout-stage-dashboard-wireframe.json
- Related design: DES-447 Audit trail view for rollout actions

Open questions
1) Do we show “auto-abort vs auto-hold” distinctly in the timeline? (Product wants clear, SRE wants explicit, customers may be alarmed.) Proposal: show in a banner + event in history; timeline node can display a small badge.
2) Does v1 support “rollback to previous stage” or only “abort to stable”? UI should not promise rollback if backend only supports abort.
3) How do we handle “manual gates” in UI? (Checkbox list vs simple acknowledgement.) Proposal: minimal v1: require reason + confirmation; add checklist later.
4) Should customers see raw query text? Proposal: no; show metrics and thresholds; keep “View query” behind internal/admin flag.
5) Gate unknown behavior: confirm fail-closed vs fail-open in UI copy. Current direction from eng thread: fail-closed + manual override.

Progress / updates (chronological)
2025-02-10 (Marissa Cole)
- Created DES-431 to unblock Console implementation. Primary asks: timeline component, gate state mapping, and messaging for hold/failure.

2025-02-14 (Kenji Nakamura)
- Drafted component states and early layout options (single-row timeline vs vertical stepper on narrow screens). Leaning horizontal + responsive wrap to preserve “phased” feel.
- Noted risk: stage/gate state confusion; will separate visuals (node fill vs gate pill).

2025-02-20 (Kenji Nakamura)
- Synced with Chloe Martin + Jada Williams on backend contract: timeline can’t infer allowed actions reliably; must trust backend flags.
- Added requirement: evidence panel must handle missing stage tags without empty state.

2025-02-26 (Review: Marissa Cole, Lauren Bishop, Rafael Mendes)
- Feedback:
  - Marissa: Make promotion CTA harder to misclick; requires confirmation and show gate summary in modal.
  - Lauren: Customers need reassurance during holds; avoid “incident-y” language.
  - Rafael: Ensure unknown telemetry is called out clearly; prefer fail-closed messaging to prevent unsafe promotes.
- Action items:
  - Add explicit “Gate status unknown” banner state.
  - Add microcopy for small pools/noisy gates.

2025-03-04 (Kenji Nakamura)
- Updated copy variants for customer vs internal views; proposed role-based content:
  - Customer admin: no query text, no mention of internal telemetry pipelines.
  - Redwood operator/internal: include staleness watermark and “View query” affordance.

2025-03-10 (Design crit)
- Decision: Keep timeline nodes compact and put details in evidence panel; avoid stacking too much info on the node.
- Decision: Gate pill on node uses icon + label on hover; always show icon to avoid color-only state.

2025-03-12 (Kenji Nakamura)
- Marked In Review pending sign-off from Product + SRE on final copy for unknown telemetry and force-promote disclaimer.

Acceptance criteria
- Stage timeline component spec covers: stage states, gate states, selection behavior, action placement, and empty/error states.
- Copy deck included for: held, gate failed, unknown telemetry, aborted, completed, force-promote confirmation.
- Clear guidance on what is customer-visible vs admin/internal-only.
- Documented expected backend fields for timeline + evidence panel.

Next steps
- Kenji: deliver final Figma and copy strings to Console team; include responsive behavior.
- Marissa/Lauren: approve customer-facing copy.
- Rafael: confirm unknown telemetry language and default policy alignment (promotion blocked).
- Chloe/Jada: confirm evidence endpoint can provide signal rows + dashboard links in v1.
